items.title: Neuroscientist: Alzheimer's Starts In Your Nose (Here’s the Fix)
items.summary: **Visit https://memoryair.com/ and use code DAVE15 for 15% off. ** Dr. Michael Leon on Smell Training, Memory, Sleep, Alzheimer’s Risk, and Brain Longevity Your sense of smell may reveal more about your brain health than you realize, and stimulating it while you sleep may improve memory, sleep quality, and cognitive function. Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Michael Leon, Professor Emeritus of Neurobiology and Behavior at UC Irvine and one of the world’s most cited scientists, to explore why smell may be one of the most overlooked tools for brain health and longevity. Dr. Leon explains why the olfactory system has unusually direct access to the brain’s memory and emotional centers, why smell often declines alongside memory after age 60, and why reduced olfactory function has been associated with Alzheimer’s disease, cognitive decline, depression, and increased all-cause mortality. They also discuss how COVID, chronic congestion, pollution, stress, and aging can impair smell without people realizing it. The conversation dives into olfactory enrichment, including research showing major improvements in memory when older adults were exposed to multiple scents during sleep. Dr. Leon explains why novelty matters, how nighttime scent exposure may increase deep sleep and reduce nightmares, and why olfactory stimulation is being studied in dementia, PTSD, depression, and autism. Dave also explores connections between smell, GLP-1 drugs, exercise, rapamycin, spermidine, oxytocin…

items.title: They Lab Tested Retatrutide — The Results Were Shocking
items.summary: Are you actually getting the peptide you paid for? In this Peptide A to Z investigation, we look at independent laboratory testing of peptide products labeled Retatrutide and NAD+ that were purchased over the counter from a Brooklyn smoke shop. Four sealed vials were tested. Two were labeled Retatrutide 10mg. Two were labeled NAD+ 500mg. 🧬 FREE PEPTIDE GUIDE: Get the Peptide A to Z Guide and learn the basics of peptides, research, terminology, and more: PeptideAtoZ.com 👥 JOIN THE PEPTIDE A TO Z COMMUNITY: Connect with others interested in peptide research, longevity, and the latest peptide science: PeptideAtoZ.com According to the reported laboratory results, none of the four samples could be positively identified as the substance stated on the label. The retatrutide samples also produced an unexpected signal that the laboratory described as suggesting “extreme contamination.” But the story gets even more concerning. CBS News separately investigated a certificate of analysis associated with the retatrutide product. The laboratory named on that certificate reportedly told CBS that it never issued the certificate and had never had the company as a client. items.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. My whole life doctors told me I'd need open heart surgery in my…

Catharine Arnston on Spirulina, Chlorella, Mitochondria, Detox, Brain Energy, and Longevity Could one of the oldest foods on Earth also be one of the most overlooked tools for mitochondrial health, brain function, detoxification, and longevity? Host Dave Asprey sits down with Catharine Arnston, founder of ENERGYbits and author of Love Your Health to Bits with Algae, to explore the biology of spirulina and chlorella and why these microscopic organisms have been studied for decades as unusually nutrient-dense foods. Catharine explains the major differences between spirulina and chlorella, from how they are grown and processed to how she uses them for completely different purposes. Spirulina contains compounds including phycocyanin and superoxide dismutase that Catharine believes can support mitochondrial function, antioxidant defenses, cellular energy, and brain health, while chlorella is used primarily for binding and removing unwanted compounds such as heavy metals. They also discuss why water quality, sourcing, drying temperature, and processing can dramatically change the final product. items.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
items.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. That could have implications extending well beyond weight loss. But there's an…

items.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
items.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. This is a perfect example of why the question isn't simply “Do peptides work?” The better question is: Which peptide, for what purpose, and where is the human evidence? 📘 FREE Peptide Guide: PeptideAtoZ.com/free-guide 💬 Join the Peptide A to Z Community: PeptideAtoZ.com/community 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research.
